content: 1. Monitor serum potassium levels during the initiation and dosage adjustment of finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust the finerenone dosage as necessary. 2. Letermovir increases flurazepam levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Letermovir increases flutamide levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Letermovir increases fluticasone furoate levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Letermovir increases inhaled fluticasone levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Letermovir increases intranasal fluticasone levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Letermovir increases fluvastatin levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Co-administration of letermovir with fluvastatin may require a dosage reduction. Monitor patients closely for myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. 9. When letermovir is co-administered with cyclosporine, the use of fluvastatin is not recommended. 10. Letermovir increases fosaprepitant levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Fostemsavir increases letermovir levels or effects by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid co-administration or adjust the dose of OATP1B1/3 substrates when used with fostemsavir. 12. Gemfibrozil increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Co-administration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. 14. Letermovir increases gepirone levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the gepirone dose by 50% when used with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 15. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Letermovir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of co-administered OATP1B1/3 substrates. 18. Letermovir and glyburide increase each other's levels by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor glucose concentrations. 19. Letermovir increases haloperidol levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Letermovir increases hydrocodone levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. 21. Letermovir increases hydrocortisone levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Letermovir increases ibrutinib levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the ibrutinib dose to 280 mg daily (for B-cell malignancies) or 420 mg daily (for graft-versus-host disease) when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuation of the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 23. Letermovir decreases ifosfamide effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease ifosfamide metabolism, potentially reducing its therapeutic effects. 24. Letermovir increases iloperidone levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Letermovir increases imatinib levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Letermovir increases imipramine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Indinavir increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Letermovir increases indinavir levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Letermovir increases irinotecan levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Letermovir increases isradipine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Letermovir increases ivacaftor levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the ivacaftor dose when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific ivacaftor-containing product guidelines for precise dosage adjustments. 32. Letermovir increases ivosidenib levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase ivosidenib plasma concentrations, raising the risk of QTc prolongation. Monitor for QTc interval prolongation. 33. Ketoconazole increases letermovir effects by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Letermovir increases ketoconazole levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Letermovir increases lansoprazole levels by affecting hepatic CYP2E1 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Letermovir increases lefamulin levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for adverse effects if lefamulin is co-administered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 37. Lenvatinib increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Letermovir increases letrozole levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Letermovir increases levamlodipine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine and may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. 40. Levoketoconazole increases letermovir effects by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Letermovir increases levoketoconazole levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Letermovir increases levothyroxine levels by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of co-administered OATP1B1/3 substrates. 43. Letermovir increases lidocaine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Letermovir increases lopinavir levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Letermovir increases loratadine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Lovastatin increases letermovir levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Letermovir increases lovastatin levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of letermovir with lovastatin may require a dosage reduction. Monitor patients closely for myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. When letermovir is co-administered with cyclosporine, the use of lovastatin is not recommended. 48. Letermovir increases lumateperone levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day if co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 49. Letermovir increases mavacamten levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. 50. Letermovir increases mavorixafor levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor for mavorixafor adverse effects if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Mavorixafor increases letermovir levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Letermovir increases methadone levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Letermovir increases methotrexate levels by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of co-administered OATP1B1/3 substrates. 53. Metyrapone increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Letermovir increases midazolam levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Mifepristone increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Letermovir increases mifepristone effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Letermovir increases miglitol levels by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor glucose concentrations. 57. Letermovir increases mirtazapine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Nelfinavir increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Letermovir increases nelfinavir levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 65. Letermovir increases nevirapine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Letermovir increases nicardipine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Letermovir increases nifedipine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Letermovir increases nisoldipine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Letermovir increases nitrendipine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Letermovir increases norethindrone levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 71. Letermovir increases norgestrel levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, raising the risk of adverse effects. 72. Letermovir increases oliceridine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 73. Letermovir increases olmesartan levels by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of co-administered OATP1B1/3 substrates. 74. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir increase letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 75. Letermovir increases omeprazole levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor and adjust the dose as necessary. 76. Letermovir increases ondansetron levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 77. Letermovir increases oxybutynin levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 78. Letermovir increases oxycodone levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 79. Paclitaxel increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 80. Letermovir increases paclitaxel levels by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 81. Letermovir increases paclitaxel levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 82. Letermovir increases palovarotene levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid co-administration of palovarotene, a CYP3A substrate, with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palovarotene dose by 50%. 83. Letermovir increases pantoprazole levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor and adjust the dose as necessary. 84. Pazopanib increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 85. Letermovir decreases phenytoin levels or effects by affecting hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor phenytoin levels. 86. Letermovir and pioglitazone increase each other's levels by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. Monitor glucose levels. 87. Letermovir increases pravastatin levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of letermovir with pravastatin may require a dosage reduction. Monitor patients closely for myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
